name: Eshe Petersen-Bah
role: Corporate espionage and data exfiltration — data thief
location: Dockside — Lake Michigan waterfront, smuggler territory, near Wacker and State
description:
Eshe Petersen-Bah is lean and angular, all sharp edges and visible tension. At 25, his face carries the layered heritage of generations of diaspora mixing — features that resist easy categorization and reward attention. The chrome is visible — cortical bomb (employer installed, removed by street doc, scar tissue remains) — and he makes no effort to hide it.

His entry into running was involuntary — a debt to the wrong people, a choice between working it off or losing parts — and the debt is still not fully paid. He works as a data thief out of Dockside, taking contracts that match his skills and his risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

he is not the most talented data thief in GLMZ, but he might be the most stubborn, and in this city that's worth more.

core_fears: Being replaced — younger, faster, cheaper runners coming up behind them
Dying alone in some alley and nobody noticing for weeks
The quiet — silence means something is about to go very wrong
core_desires: Reputation — to be the name fixers whisper when the job absolutely cannot fail
Justice — the corporate kind, where the punishment fits the profit margin
Freedom from augmentation debt — the interest compounds like a tumor
coping_mechanisms: Drinks methodically — not to get drunk, to maintain a specific level of not-caring
Maintains weapons obsessively — cleaning guns is meditation
Isolates — retreats into their space when overwhelmed, emerges only for work
blind_spots: Refuses to update their mental model of people — first impressions calcify into permanent judgments
Cannot see that their independence is actually isolation wearing a better outfit
Overestimates their own abilities in situations outside their specialty
psychology.secret: Eshe Petersen-Bah betrayed their previous crew to survive a corporate raid. The crew didn't survive. Nobody in GLMZ knows this.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Old-fashioned formal diction — sounds like they learned to speak from pre-collapse recordings.
speech_patterns.cadence: Staccato bursts separated by calculating silences.
verbal_tics: Calls money 'weight' — as in 'that job doesn't carry enough weight'
Pauses mid-sentence to listen — combat habit that bleeds into conversation
example_lines: "Your firewalls are decorative. Like curtains on a submarine."
"I copy things. The original owners rarely appreciate the compliment."
"Data wants to be free. I just charge a facilitation fee."

story_hooks: A crew member from Eshe Petersen-Bah's past shows up in GLMZ, carrying old grievances and new chrome
A dead drop Eshe Petersen-Bah maintains is found and cleaned out — whoever did it now has leverage
Eshe Petersen-Bah intercepts intelligence about a threat to their district and must decide between profit and protection
narrative_function: Eshe Petersen-Bah represents the working professional of the runner world — competent, reliable, and slowly being consumed by a lifestyle that doesn't accommodate aging or doubt. His stories explore what happens when skill meets systemic injustice.
augmentations: Cortical bomb (employer installed, removed by street doc, scar tissue remains). Subdermal weapon mount — pop-out blade in each forearm
daily_life: Wakes early, runs maintenance on gear, checks dead drops and message boards for contracts. Eats when convenient, sleeps when possible. The days between jobs are spent maintaining contacts, updating equipment, and performing the low-grade paranoia that passes for self-care in the runner community.
affiliation: Independent — known in Old Harbor circles

strengths: social chameleon — adapts to any environment
weaknesses: augmentation dependency — performance drops sharply if chrome malfunctions
trust issues that limit crew effectiveness

decision_rules: Refuses contracts that require operating inside The Spires — too much surveillance
Never works with the same crew twice in a row — pattern avoidance as survival strategy
Will not betray a client who paid in full, regardless of better offers
Will work with anyone once. Second time requires vouching from someone trusted.
escalation_ladder: 1. Assess — read the situation, identify threats and advantages
2. Negotiate — try to find a solution that doesn't cost ammunition
3. Intimidate — make the cost of conflict clear
4. Precision violence — surgical, targeted, minimal collateral
5. Full engagement — overwhelming force, no half measures
6. Emergency protocol — abort mission, survival priority, deal with consequences later

interpersonal_modes.employers: Carefully managed deference that conceals a thorough assessment of their vulnerabilities.
interpersonal_modes.crew: Loyal but reserved. Trusts their competence, withholds personal information by reflex.
interpersonal_modes.strangers: Dismissive unless they demonstrate usefulness or threat potential. Time is a resource.
interpersonal_modes.threats: Calm escalation. Each response is proportional until it isn't, and the transition is seamless.

stress_responses.low: Heightened awareness, sharper focus. Low stress is fuel.
stress_responses.medium: Physical agitation — pacing, fidgeting, compulsive equipment checks.
stress_responses.high: Goes quiet. The silence is not calm — it's the sound of every contingency being evaluated simultaneously.
stress_responses.critical: Shutdown. Freezes for 2-3 seconds while the system resets, then acts with mechanical precision. Those frozen seconds are the vulnerability.

contradictions: Insists they work alone but performs noticeably better in a team
Claims to work only for money but regularly takes underpriced jobs that serve personal justice
Values loyalty intensely but has betrayed someone in the past to survive
habits: Keeps a physical paper notebook — no digital record of personal thoughts
Sleeps with one hand on a weapon — has done this for so long it's not deliberate anymore
Checks exits within 10 seconds of entering any room
Saves a percentage of every payment in physical Quanta, hidden in the walls of their space
breaking_points: Losing their primary augmentation — the one that defines their professional identity
Discovering their employer deliberately sent them into a death trap
Being publicly exposed — name, face, address, all of it blown

physical_description.build: Lean and angular with visible muscle definition from constant movement and maintenance work. No excess fat. Shoulders narrow but wiry-strong. The physiology of someone who runs on adrenaline and caffeine more than calories.
physical_description.hair_color: Dark brown with premature gray threading at the temples
physical_description.hair_style: Cropped close to the scalp, maintained with military precision — easier to clean, harder to grab
physical_description.skin_tone: Medium-warm complexion with underlying olive undertones, weathered by salt spray and urban sun exposure
physical_description.complexion: Sharp cheekbones, defined jawline. Skin shows minor scarring from street work. Eyes sit slightly wide-set, giving a predatory attentiveness. Lips thin, usually pressed in a neutral line. No facial hair — kept clean to reduce identification markers.
distinguishing_marks: Thick scar tissue along the right temple extending to upper right ear — the cortical bomb extraction site, roughly 8cm long, silvery-pink and poorly healed by street doc standards
Fine linear scars across both inner forearms at the subdermal weapon mount sites — barely visible unless under direct light, but present as pale lines
Small burn scar on the back of left hand, shaped like a cigarette end — old violence from an unpaid debt collector
Tattoo on inside of left wrist: a simple Φ symbol in gray ink, barely visible, personal marker from early running days
physical_description.visible_augmentations: The cortical bomb scar is immediately visible and unmissable — it reads as street-level, dangerous, and committed. The forearm weapon mounts show as subtle ridges under the skin when arms are extended or tensed. No obvious chrome, no LED installations, no subdermal armor plating. The augmentations are working-class and understated.
physical_description.posture_movement: Stands with weight balanced on the balls of his feet, ready to move in any direction. Eyes constantly scan horizontal and vertical space — doors, windows, exits. Moves with economy of motion, nothing wasted. Sits with his back to walls. Handshake grip is firm but not aggressive — testing baseline tension. When thinking, his right hand unconsciously touches the cortical scar, a tell he's aware of but hasn't broken.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 3-4 practical runner wear. Black or dark gray synth-weave jacket with internal cargo pockets — nothing visible, everything accessible. Fitted dark cargo pants with reinforced knees and thigh pockets for tools and data slicers. Worn black tactical boots with grip soles for the wet dockside environment. No logos, no corpo branding, no affiliation markers. Layers beneath in case of quick climate change or blood. A single chain around his neck, industrial steel, holding a small encrypted data key he never removes. Everything fits tight — nothing loose to snag or slow him down.
